judged_text: The no-credentialId fallback branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the externalId argument, so CalendarManager returns externalId: undefined and the BookingReference built from that result stores externalCalendarId: undefined where the old code stored evt.destinationCalendar.externalId. Events created through this path are recorded in references with no calendar id, so later reschedule/cancel cannot locate the calendar — combined with Google's dead fallback this strands the event permanently on whatever calendar it was created on, leaving ghost events after cancellation.

Events created through this path are recorded in references with no calendar id, so later reschedule/cancel cannot locate the calendar — combined with Google's dead fallback this strands the event permanently on whatever calendar it was created on, leaving ghost events after cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `event.destinationCalendar` entries that *lack* `credentialId`, the code falls into the `else` branch and does `destinationCalendarCredentials.map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event))` (no `destination.externalId` passed). But `CalendarManager.createEvent` was changed to optionally return `externalId` and `EventManager` now records `externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId` (not from `evt.destinationCalendar`). Therefore this path will produce references with `externalCalendarId: undefined`. This is a regression vs the old behavior where references used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The diff also shows Google `createEvent` now selects calendar by matching `credentialId`, so when the destination entry has no `credentialId`, it will likely fall back to `primary`, making later update/delete unable to target the correct calendar.
